paragraphs: Corning traces its origins to a glass business established in 1851. The present corporation was incorporated in the State of New York in December 1936. The Company's name was changed from Corning Glass Works to Corning Incorporated on April 28, 1989.

Corning is vital to progress – in the industries we help advance and in the world we share. With a 175-year track record of life-changing inventions, Corning applies its unparalleled expertise in glass science, ceramic science and optical physics, along with its deep manufacturing and engineering capabilities to develop category-defining products that transform industries and enhance people's lives. Our materials science and manufacturing expertise, boundless curiosity and commitment to purposeful invention place us at the center of the way the world works, learns and lives. In addition, our sustained investment in research, development and engineering capabilities means we are always ready to solve the toughest challenges alongside our customers.

Our capabilities are versatile and synergistic, allowing Corning to evolve to meet changing market needs, while also helping customers capture new opportunities in dynamic industries. Today, Corning's markets include optical communications, display, mobile consumer electronics, automotive, life sciences, semiconductors and solar. Corning's industry-leading products include damage-resistant cover materials for mobile devices; precision glass for advanced displays; optical fiber, cable and connectivity solutions for advanced communications networks, such as fiber to the home and data centers, enabling artificial intelligence and connections around the world; trusted products to accelerate drug discovery and delivery; and clean-air technologies and technical glass for cars and trucks.
Corning manufactures products in 14 countries and operates in five reportable segments: Optical Communications, Display, Specialty Materials, Automotive and Life Sciences.

As of January 1, 2025, the Company began managing its Automotive Glass Solutions business together with its Environmental Technologies business, forming its Automotive segment, and its Display Technologies segment was renamed to "Display."
The comparative period segment information presented herein has been recast to reflect the above changes in segment reporting.

We invented the world's first low-loss optical fiber in 1970. Since that milestone, we have continued to pioneer optical fiber, cable and connectivity solutions. As global demand driven by video usage grows exponentially, telecommunications networks continue to migrate from copper to optical-based systems that can deliver the required cost-effective capacity. Additionally, the rapid acceleration of artificial intelligence ("AI") is driving strong demand for fiber and connectivity products inside and between data centers. Our experience puts us in a unique position to design and deliver optical solutions that reach every edge of the communications network.

The Optical Communications segment is divided into two main product groupings – carrier network and enterprise network. The carrier network group consists primarily of products and solutions for optical-based communications infrastructure for services such as video, data and voice communications. The enterprise network group consists primarily of optical-based communication networks sold to businesses, governments and individuals for their own use.

Our carrier network product portfolio encompasses an array of optical fiber products, including Vascade® optical fibers for use in submarine networks; LEAF® optical fiber for long-haul, regional and metropolitan networks; SMF-28e® ULL and TXF® fiber for more scalable long-haul and regional networks; SMF-28e+™ single-mode optical fiber providing additional transmission wavelengths in metropolitan and access networks and ClearCurve® ultra-bendable single-mode fiber for use in multiple-dwelling units and fiber-to-the-home applications. For high performance across the range of long-haul, metro, access and fiber-to-the-home network applications, SMF-28e® Ultra and SMF-28e® Contour fibers deliver industry-leading attenuation, compatibility and improved

macrobend performance in one fiber. A portion of our optical fiber is sold directly to end users and third-party cablers globally. Our remaining fiber production is cabled internally and sold to end users as either bulk cable or as part of an integrated optical solution. Our cable products, including the RocketRibbon® and miniXtend® portfolios, support various outdoor, indoor/outdoor and indoor applications and include a broad range of loose tube, ribbon and drop cable designs with flame-retardant versions available for indoor and indoor/outdoor use.

In addition to optical fiber and cable, our carrier network product portfolio also includes hardware and equipment products, including cable assemblies, fiber-optic hardware, fiber-optic connectors, optical components and couplers, closures, network interface devices and other accessories. These products may be sold as individual components or as part of integrated optical connectivity solutions designed for various carrier network applications. Examples of these solutions include our Evolv™ platform, which provides pre-connectorized solutions for cost-effectively deploying fiber-to-the-home and 5G networks; and the Centrix platform, which provides a fiber management system with industry-leading density and innovative jumper routing that can be deployed in a wide variety of carrier switching centers.

Our enterprise network portfolio leverages optical fiber products, including ClearCurve® ultra-bendable multimode fiber for private and hyperscale data centers and other enterprise network applications.

Our hardware and equipment for enterprise network applications include cable assemblies, fiber-optic hardware, fiber-optic connectors, optical components and couplers, closures and other accessories. These products may be sold as individual components or as part of integrated optical connectivity solutions designed for various network applications, including hyperscale data centers. Examples of enterprise network solutions include the Edge8® platform, which provides high-density pre-connectorized cabling solutions for data center applications, supporting a path to speeds of 400G and beyond.

We invented new fibers, cables and connectors to capture the generative AI enterprise demand. This includes our SMF-28e® Contour fiber, a 40% smaller fiber delivering improved bend resistance in high-density environments. This fiber forms the basis of our Contour Flow™ Cable, which can fit double the fiber into the same cable diameter. These components are being adopted by hyperscale data centers as well as the carriers building data center interconnect networks, and others focusing on key technology vectors such as density, latency and sustainability.

paragraphs: We operate globally in a rapidly changing economic, political and technological environment that presents numerous risks. Our operations and financial results are subject to risks and uncertainties, including those described below, that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, our ability to successfully execute our strategy and the trading price of our common stock or debt. The following discussion identifies the most significant factors that may adversely affect the Company. This information should be read in conjunction with Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Conditions and Results of Operations ("MD&A") and the consolidated financial statements and related notes incorporated by reference into this report. The following discussion of risks is not all inclusive but is designed to highlight what we believe are important factors to consider, as these factors could cause our future results to differ from those in our forward-looking statements and from historical trends.

Inflationary price pressures and uncertain availability of commodities, raw materials, utilities, labor or other inputs used by us and our suppliers, or instability in logistics and related costs, among other factors, could negatively impact our profitability

Increases in the price of commodities, raw materials, utilities, labor or other inputs that we or our suppliers use in manufacturing and supplying products, components and parts, along with logistics and other related costs, may lead to higher production and shipping costs for our products, parts and components. Further, increasing global demand for, and uncertain supply of, such materials could disrupt our or our suppliers' ability to obtain such materials in a timely manner to meet our supply needs and/or could lead to increased costs. Any increase in the cost of inputs to our production could lead to higher costs for our products and could negatively impact our operating results, future profitability and ability to successfully deliver on our strategy. Increasing our prices to our customers may cause certain of our customers to push out, cancel or refrain from purchasing our products, which could materially adversely impact demand for our products, and thereby also negatively impact our operating results, future profitability and ability to successfully deliver on our strategy.

Factors such as supply chain disruptions, manufacturing interruptions or delays, or the failure to accurately forecast customer demand, could affect our ability to meet customer demand, lead to higher costs, or result in excess or obsolete inventory; if we are unable to obtain the necessary equipment, raw and batch materials, natural resources, utilities and other essentials required in our products or processes, our business will be negatively impacted

Corning's business relies on the timely supply of raw materials, precious metals, natural resources or utilities including energy and industrial water, equipment, parts and components, services and related products to meet the changing technical and volume requirements of its customers, which depends in part on the timely delivery of materials, equipment and services, from suppliers and contract manufacturers. Significant or sudden increases in demand for such materials, equipment and services, as well as delays in and unpredictability of shipments due to transportation interruptions, have resulted in, and may continue to result in, a shortage of materials, equipment and services needed to manufacture Corning's products. Such shortages have adversely impacted, and may continue to adversely impact, our suppliers' ability to meet our demand requirements and Corning's manufacturing operations and its ability to meet customer demand. Some key materials, equipment and services are subject to long lead-times or are available only from a single supplier or limited group of suppliers and we may not be able to find alternate sources in a timely manner. Volatility of demand for manufacturing equipment can increase capital, technical, operational and other risks for Corning and for companies throughout our supply chain, and may cause some suppliers to exit businesses, scale back or cease operations, which could impact our ability to meet customer demand and could have a material adverse effect on our business.

Corning's industry-leading products include damage-resistant cover materials for mobile devices; precision glass for advanced displays; optical fiber, cable and connectivity solutions for advanced communications networks, such as fiber to the home and data centers, enabling artificial intelligence and connections around the world; trusted products to accelerate drug discovery and delivery; and clean-air technologies and technical glass for cars and trucks.

In the third quarter of 2023, we introduced our Springboard plan to grow sales and enhance our profitability base. We communicated a high-confidence plan to add $3 billion in incremental annualized core sales by the end of 2026 (as compared to our Springboard starting point), and in March 2025 we upgraded this high-confidence plan to $4 billion. We also set a core operating margin target of 20% by the end of 2026. The fourth quarter of 2025 marked the second anniversary of our Springboard plan, and we believe it has been a tremendous success to date. Since its launch, we have added significant annualized core sales and expanded our core operating margin, and as of the fourth quarter of 2025, we achieved both our growth and profitability targets a full year ahead of plan. Our achievement of both of these key milestones ahead of schedule serves as an example of how we have transformed the Company's financial profile over the last two years. Overall, we believe we have established a firm foundation from which to launch future profitable growth. We see remarkable demand for our innovations and manufacturing capabilities, which we believe will lead to additional growth opportunities through 2026 and beyond. We therefore expect to increase both our capacity and technology capabilities as required to achieve our goals, while sharing risk appropriately to achieve the returns that underpin our Springboard plan.
For the first quarter of 2026, we expect core net sales in the range of approximately $4.2 billion to $4.3 billion.
The following table presents selected highlights from our operations (in millions): Year ended December 31, % change

Net sales for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $2.5 billion, or 19%, when compared to the same period in 2024. The increase was primarily driven by an increase in sales for optical communications products of $1.6 billion, polycrystalline silicon products and solar module sales of $348 million, display products of $238 million, specialty material products of $194 million and automotive products of $73 million. Refer to the "Segment Analysis" section of our MD&A below for a discussion of net sales by segment.
In 2025 and 2024, sales in international markets accounted for 57% and 61% of total net sales, respectively.

The types of expenses included in cost of sales are: raw materials consumption, including direct and indirect materials; salaries, wages and benefits; depreciation and amortization; production utilities; production-related purchasing; warehousing (including receiving and inspection); repairs and maintenance; inter-location inventory transfer costs; production and warehousing facility property insurance; rent for production facilities; freight and logistics costs; and other production overhead.

Cost of sales increased by $1.2 billion, or 13%, when compared to the same period in 2024, primarily driven by the increase in net sales, as discussed above. Gross margin increased by $1.3 billion, or 31% and gross margin as a percentage of net sales increased by 3 percentage points when compared to 2024 driven by higher volume and the impact of actions taken by management to improve profitability, including raising prices, reducing costs and increasing productivity.

The types of expenses included in selling, general and administrative expenses are: salaries, wages and benefits, including variable compensation and share-based compensation expense; travel; sales commissions; professional fees; and depreciation and amortization, utilities and rent for administrative facilities.

paragraphs: Corning 來源可追溯至 1851 年成立的玻璃業務。目前的公司於 1936 年 12 月在紐約州註冊成立。本公司於 1989 年 4 月 28 日將公司名稱由 Corning Glass Works 改為 Corning Incorporated。

Corning 對進步至關重要 – 在我們協助推動的產業中，以及在我們共同生活的世界中。擁有 175 年改變生命的發明歷史，Corning 以其在玻璃科學、陶瓷科學與光學物理領域無與倫比的專業知識，搭配深厚的製造與工程能力，開發出定義產業的產品，轉變產業並提升人們的生活品質。我們的材料科學與製造專業知識、無限的好奇心與致力於有意義發明的承諾，使我們處於世界運作、學習與生活的中心。此外，我們持續投資於研究、開發與工程能力，意味著我們始終準備好與客戶共同解決最困難的挑戰。

我們的專業能力多樣且具有協同效應，使 Corning 能夠因應變動的市場需求而進化，同時協助客戶在動態產業中把握新的機會。目前，Corning 的市場包括光通信、顯示、行動消費電子、汽車、生命科學、半導體與太陽能。Corning 的產業領先產品包括行動裝置的抗損蓋材、用於先進顯示的精準玻璃、光纖、電纜與連接解決方案，用於先進通訊網路，例如光纖到家與資料中心，使人工智慧與全球連線成為可能；加速藥物發現與遞送的可信產品；以及用於汽車與卡車的潔淨空氣技術與技術玻璃。
Corning 在 14 個國家製造產品，並運作於五個應報告分部：光通信、顯示、特殊材料、汽車與生命科學。
自 2025 年 1 月 1 日起，本公司開始將其汽車玻璃解決方案業務與環境技術業務共同管理，形成其汽車分部，並將其顯示科技分部更名為 "顯示"。
本文件中提供的比較期間分部資訊已重新整理，以反映上述分部報告的變更。
我們於 1970 年發明瞭世界上第一根低損耗光纖。自那項里程碑後，我們持續開拓光纖、電纜與連接解決方案。隨著視訊使用需求指數成長，通訊網路持續從銅線遷移至光基系統，以提供所需的成本效益容量。此外，人工智慧（"AI"）的快速發展正在推動資料中心內外對光纖與連接產品的強勁需求。我們的經驗使我們處於獨特的位置，能設計並交付達成通訊網路每一個邊緣的光學解決方案。
光通信分部可分為兩個主要產品羣組 – 電信網路與企業網路。電信網路羣組主要由用於視訊、資料與語音通訊等光基通訊基礎設施的產品與解決方案組成。企業網路羣組主要由銷售給企業、政府與個人用以自行使用的光基通訊網路組成。

本公司電信業者網路產品組合包含一系列光纖產品，包括用於海底網路的 Vascade® 光纖；用於長途、區域及都會網路的 LEAF® 光纖；用於更具擴展性的長途及區域網路的 SMF-28e® ULL 和 TXF® 光纖；用於都會及接入網路並提供額外傳輸波長的 SMF-28e+™ 單模光纖；以及用於多戶住宅及光纖到家應用的 ClearCurve® 超柔單模光纖。為在長途、都會、接入及光纖到家網路應用中實現高性能，SMF-28e® Ultra 和 SMF-28e® Contour 光纖提供業界領先的衰減、相容性及改善的宏觀彎曲性能。本公司部分光纖產品直接銷售給終端用戶及全球第三方電纜廠商。本公司剩餘的光纖生產則 internally cabled 並銷售給終端用戶，作為 bulk cable 或整合光纖解決方案的一部分。本公司電纜產品，包括 RocketRibbon® 和 miniXtend® 系列，支援各種戶外、室內/戶外及室內應用，並包含一系列鬆套管、ribbon 及 drop cable 設計，並有阻燃版本可供室內及室內/戶外使用。

除了光纖及電纜，本公司電信業者網路產品組合亦包含硬體及設備產品，包括電纜組裝、光纖硬體、光纖連接器、光學零組件及耦合器、封裝、網路介面設備及其他配件。這些產品可作為單一零組件銷售，或作為整合光纖連接解決方案銷售，用於各種電信業者網路應用。這些解決方案的範例包括本公司 Evolv™ 平台，提供預連接解決方案，以低成本部署光纖到家及 5G 網路；以及 Centrix 平台，提供光纖管理系統，具有業界領先的密度及創新跳線佈線，可廣泛應用於各種電信業者交換中心。

除了光纖及電纜，本公司電信業者網路產品組合亦包含硬體及設備產品，包括電纜組裝、光纖硬體、光纖連接器、光學零組件及耦合器、封裝、網路介面設備及其他配件。這些產品可作為單一零組件銷售，或作為整合光纖連接解決方案銷售，用於各種電信業者網路應用。這些解決方案的範例包括本公司 Evolv™ 平台，提供預連接解決方案，以低成本部署光纖到家及 5G 網路；以及 Centrix 平台，提供光纖管理系統，具有業界領先的密度及創新跳線佈線，可廣泛應用於各種電信業者交換中心。
本公司企業網路產品組合運用光纖產品，包括 ClearCurve® 超柔 bendable 多模光纖，用於私人及超規模資料中心及其他企業網路應用。
本公司企業網路應用的硬體與設備包括電纜組裝、光纖硬體、光纖連接器、光學零組件與耦合器、封裝與其他配件。這些產品可能以單一零組件方式販售，或作為整合光學連接解決方案的一部分，用於各種網路應用，包括超規模資料中心。企業網路解決方案的範例包括 Edge8® 平台，該平台提供高密度預連接電纜解決方案，用於資料中心應用，支援 400G 及更高速度的連接。

本公司發明瞭新的光纖、電纜與連接器，以捕捉生成式 AI 企業需求。這包括我們的 SMF-28e® Contour 光纖，這是一種體積較小 40% 的光纖，在高密度環境中提供改進的彎曲抗性。此光纖是本公司 Contour Flow™ 電纜的基礎，該電纜可在相同電纜直徑內容納雙倍的光纖。這些零組件已被超規模資料中心以及建設資料中心互連網路的電信業者，以及其他專注於密度、延遲與永續性等關鍵技術方向的企業所採用。

康寧對進步至關重要 – 在我們協助推動的產業中，以及在我們共同生活的世界中。憑藉 175 年的改變生命的發明歷史，康寧運用其無與倫比的玻璃科學、陶瓷科學與光學物理專業知識，以及深厚的製造與工程能力，開發出定義產業的產品，轉變產業並提升人們的生活。我們的材料科學與製造專業知識、無限的好奇心以及對有意義發明的承諾，使我們處於世界運作、學習與生活的中心。此外，我們持續投資於研究、開發與工程能力，意味著我們始終準備好與客戶共同解決最困難的挑戰。

我們的專業能力多樣且具有協同效應，使康寧能夠適應變動的市場需求，同時協助客戶在動態產業中抓住新機會。目前，康寧的市場包括光通信、顯示、行動消費電子、汽車、生命科學、半導體與太陽能。康寧的產業領導產品包括行動裝置的抗損蓋材、用於先進顯示的精準玻璃、光纖、電纜與連接解決方案，用於先進通訊網路，例如光纖到家與資料中心，以啟動人工智慧與全球連線；加速藥物發現與遞送的可信產品；以及用於汽車與卡車的潔淨空氣技術與技術玻璃。

在 2023 年第三季，我們推出了 Springboard 計畫，以增加銷售並強化我們的獲利基礎。我們宣佈了一項高信心計畫，預計到 2026 年底（相較於 Springboard 起點）每年增加 30 億美元的核心銷售額，並在 2025 年 3 月將此高信心計畫提升至 40 億美元。我們也設定了到 2026 年底核心營運毛利目標為 20%。2025 年第四季是我們 Springboard 計畫的第二週年，我們認為到目前為止此計畫已取得巨大成功。自計畫啟動以來，我們已增加大量年度核心銷售額並擴大核心營運毛利，截至 2025 年第四季，我們已提前一年達成成長與獲利目標。我們提前達成這兩個關鍵里程碑，顯示我們在過去兩年內已轉變公司的財務面貌。總體而言，我們認為已建立穩固的基礎，以發動未來的獲利成長。我們看到對我們創新與製造能力的顯著需求，我們相信這將帶來至 2026 年及以後的更多成長機會。因此，我們預期將根據需要增加我們的產能與技術能力，同時適當地分享風險，以實現 Springboard 計畫所奠基的回報。
對於 2026 年第一季，我們預期核心淨銷售額約在 42 億至 43 億美元之間。

淨銷售額於 2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度較 2024 年同期增加 $25 億，或 19%。此增加主要來自光通訊產品銷售增加 $16 億，多晶矽產品及太陽能模組銷售增加 $3.48 億，顯示產品銷售增加 $2.38 億，特殊材料產品銷售增加 $1.94 億，以及汽車產品銷售增加 $0.73 億。請參閱我們 MD&A 下方的 "分部分析" 節，以瞭解各分部的淨銷售額討論。
2025 年及 2024 年，國際市場銷售佔總淨銷售額的 57% 及 61%。
成本中包含的費用類型為：原材料消耗，包括直接及間接材料；薪資、工資及福利；折舊及攤銷；生產電力；生產相關採購；倉儲（包括進貨及檢驗）；維修及保養；跨地區存貨轉移成本；生產及倉儲設施財產保險；生產設施租金；運輸及物流成本；及其他生產間接費用。
成本增加 $12 億，或 13%，較 2024 年同期增加，主要由於淨銷售額增加，如上所述。毛利增加 $13 億，或 31%，且毛利佔淨銷售額百分比增加 3 個百分點，較 2024 年增加，因於提高產量及管理層採取行動改善獲利能力，包括提高價格、降低成本及提高生產力的影響。
銷售、一般及行政費用中包含的費用類型為：薪資、工資及福利，包括變動報酬及股票報酬費用；旅行；銷售佣金；專業費用；及折舊及攤銷、行政設施的電力及租金。

paragraphs: 本公司在全球快速變動的經濟、政治與科技環境中運作，此環境中存在許多風險。本公司之營運與財務結果受風險與不確定性影響，包括下文所述之風險，這些風險可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流、成功執行本公司策略以及普通股或債務之交易價格產生不利影響。下文討論識別出最重大之因素，這些因素可能對本公司產生不利影響。此資訊應與管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析（"MD&A"）以及合併財務報表及相關附註（已納入本報告）一併閱讀。下文所述之風險並非全部，但係設計用以強調本公司認為重要之因素，因為這些因素可能導致未來結果與本公司之預測性陳述及歷史趨勢不同。
通貨膨脹導致之價格壓力以及商品、原材料、公用設施、勞動力或其他投入物之供應不確定性，或物流與相關成本之不穩定，等因素，可能對本公司之獲利能力產生負面影響

本公司或其供應商在製造與供應產品、零組件與零件時所使用之商品、原材料、公用設施、勞動力或其他投入物之價格上漲，以及物流與其他相關成本之增加，可能導致本公司產品、零件與零組件之生產與運輸成本提高。此外，全球對這些材料之需求增加，以及供應之不確定性，可能幹擾本公司或其供應商及時取得這些材料以滿足本公司之供應需求，或導致成本增加。任何投入物之成本增加，可能導致本公司產品成本提高，並對本公司營運結果、未來獲利能力及成功執行策略之能力產生負面影響。提高本公司對客戶之價格，可能導致部分客戶延後、取消或放棄購買本公司產品，這可能對本公司產品之需求產生重大不利影響，進而對本公司營運結果、未來獲利能力及成功執行策略之能力產生負面影響。
供應鏈中斷、製造中斷或延誤，或未能準確預測客戶需求等因素，可能影響本公司滿足客戶需求之能力，導致成本提高，或造成過多或過時之存貨；若本公司無法取得製造產品或過程所需之必要設備、原材料與批次材料、天然資源、公用設施及其他必需品，將對本公司業務產生負面影響

康寧之業務依賴於原材料、貴重金屬、天然資源或公用設施（包括能源與工業用水）、設備、零件與零組件、服務及相關產品之及時供應，以符合客戶變動之技術與數量需求，此需求部分取決於供應商與合同製造商之及時交付材料、設備與服務。對這些材料、設備與服務之需求顯著或突然增加，以及因運輸中斷導致之交付延誤與不可預測性，已導致並可能繼續導致製造康寧產品所需之材料、設備與服務之短缺。這些短缺已對本公司供應商滿足本公司需求之能力及康寧之製造作業與其滿足客戶需求之能力產生不利影響，並可能繼續產生不利影響。某些關鍵材料、設備與服務受長交貨週期或僅能從單一供應商或有限供應商羣組取得，本公司可能無法在合理時間內尋找替代來源。製造設備需求之波動可能增加康寧及其供應鏈中其他公司之資本、技術、營運及其他風險，並可能導致部分供應商退出業務、縮減規模或停止營運，這可能影響本公司滿足客戶需求之能力，並可能對本公司業務產生重大不利影響。
康寧也可能因以下原因而經驗到製造作業之重大中斷、交付產品或服務之延誤、成本增加或客戶訂單取消：
